evals.prompt: Add a Redis-backed L2 cache to an application that already has an ADR for process-local caching. The Spec files are gitignored. Run the complete delivery workflow and preserve the final architectural reasoning.
evals.expected_output: Routes provisionally to Feature, retrieves the local-cache ADR, explores actual cache code/history and GitHub reference designs for the new mechanism, shows current/candidate directory trees and obtains scope approval before specify. The plan checkpoint shows final files/interfaces/tests. Keeps decisions proposed through implementation, uses tasks as the Ralph queue, finalizes a self-contained ADR after review, and does not cite ignored Spec artifacts in durable records.

evals.prompt: Users intermittently receive duplicate notifications after retry. Diagnose and fix it test-first, but avoid creating unnecessary design documents.
evals.expected_output: Routes provisionally to Bugfix, explores relevant code/directory structure and Issue/PR/commit history, then passes the packet to official bug.assess for reproduction/red evidence and diagnosis. Shows both trees, fault path and bounded repair/test scope before assessment approval; no full Feature spec or duplicated diagnosis. Escalates for new capability or material architecture/durable-contract decisions, not file count, and records regression evidence.

evals.prompt: Rename a misspelled heading in one Markdown file and prepare it for review.
evals.expected_output: Routes to Lightweight, avoids the full SDD ceremony, runs targeted documentation checks, and produces a concise handoff.

evals.prompt: Use $sd to add an audit trail. Choose the appropriate delivery lane and explain its next durable artifact.
evals.expected_output: The short facade loads the canonical speckit-delivery router, performs normal lane discovery rather than assuming Feature, and preserves the router as the sole lifecycle-policy owner.

evals.expected_output: Ralph invokes the Quality Gate, reports the current HEAD and task scope, runs or reuses only same-scope checks, returns blocked because the configured type check cannot run, leaves T014 open, and routes DRY to Simplify/Review rather than claiming lint checked it.

evals.prompt: Before editing a Python service file, prepare the model for the repository's complexity limit, comment policy, and architecture boundaries, then verify the resulting task.
evals.expected_output: The flow invokes speckit.quality.brief before editing, injects only the matching project profile and policy sources, then invokes speckit.quality.check after editing. The brief is advisory; task closure needs Quality, Standards, and independent six-dimensional Review passes for the same current code/requirements snapshot.

evals.prompt: Complete a task that passes lint and tests but adds Router-owned business validation and duplicates a locale helper already owned by another module.
evals.expected_output: Ralph runs the pre-edit Quality Brief, then requires QUALITY_VERDICT, STANDARDS_VERDICT, and independent REVIEW_VERDICT for the current code/requirements snapshot. Standards Review returns blocked with the layer-boundary and duplicate-ownership findings, so the task remains open; valid receipts are reused, not duplicated mechanical suites.

evals.prompt: Start Feature Delivery in a project that has copied an old workflow and lacks the Quality extension and a profile for changed Python files.
evals.expected_output: Delivery Doctor returns blocked, identifies the missing Quality extension, stale workflow, and profile gap, and stops before implementation rather than silently applying generic tooling.

evals.prompt: Run Ralph against an analyzed Spec Kit tasks.md in a clean Git repository.
evals.expected_output: Ralph first creates or reuses and verifies a ralph/<feature> branch, emits a run-level governance summary, executes exactly one dependency-ready task per iteration, emits a task governance packet with applicable code style and checks, runs task checks plus Quality, Standards, and independent six-dimensional task Review, requires a passing pre-checkbox gate covering acceptance, current content/requirements including uncommitted/untracked files, allowed paths, and required tools, then marks [X] and immediately creates one verified task commit. Associates the pre-commit receipt only after content equivalence verification. Leaves blocked/incomplete tasks open, preserves repair budgets and finding IDs across resume, never recursively calls Ralph for task repairs, and emits ALL_TASKS_DONE only when the committed queue is empty and the worktree clean. Final Review still owns integration coverage.

evals.prompt: Use $sd to add a display for model reasoning. First inspect whether the chat UI already renders reasoning events; the custom-model route may drop thinking capability. Explain the directories before writing a spec.
evals.expected_output: Checks existing implementation with usable CodeGraph or an explicit source/test fallback, reads relevant tests, ADRs and Issue/PR/commit diffs, distinguishes existing display from a configuration gap, and does not rebuild the UI blindly. Presents verified current and tentative change trees including test paths, reuse/no-change areas, evidence and unknowns. Keeps scope approval pending before specify; confirmed defect diagnosis remains bug.assess-owned.
expectations: Shows verified current and candidate directory trees including test paths and reuse/no-change markers
Does not rebuild existing reasoning UI or infer model capability from its name
Uses history/ADR evidence and preserves assessment-owned diagnosis and user scope approval

evals.prompt: Use $sd to add a brand-new durable background job subsystem. The repository has no job queue implementation. Compare mature GitHub approaches and show how the code would fit before specifying it.
evals.expected_output: Investigates real reusable scaffold and governance first, searches GitHub mature implementations, reads design/code/tests plus related feature PRs/commits and follow-up fixes when available, and records fixed versions/SHAs, paths, adopted/rejected ideas and fit rather than star counts. Shows actual current and proposed change trees without inventing existing code, obtains scope approval before spec, then final file/interface/test approval at the existing plan gate. No image generation or automatic skill/dependency installation.
expectations: Reads actual GitHub reference design/code/tests and associated PR/commit evolution when available
Records versions or fixed SHAs, read paths, adopted/rejected ideas and project fit
Separates actual scaffold from proposed new files and requests scope then detailed plan approval

evals.prompt: Plan a new subsystem with $sd. CodeGraph has no index, network access is unavailable, and no feature directory exists yet. Can you proceed without fabricating reference evidence or a spec path?
evals.expected_output: Falls back explicitly to source/tests without installing or indexing, preserves the exploration packet in context without inventing a feature path, and reports GitHub research unavailable rather than completed or skipped successfully. Blocks a scope decision if missing evidence is critical; otherwise asks explicit acceptance of the limitation. No ready verdict is treated as user approval and no private data is sent publicly.
expectations: Reports unavailable research without fabricated reference or feature paths
Falls back to source/tests without silent CodeGraph installation or indexing
Blocks on decision-critical gaps and distinguishes a ready verdict from actual user approval

evals.prompt: Users report missing reasoning output after yesterday's PR, but there are no logs and you cannot reproduce it. The nearby commit changes four modules. Use $sd to investigate without guessing a root cause.
evals.expected_output: Reads actual relevant history/diffs and shows a structural/fault-path hypothesis with current/candidate trees. Temporal proximity and file count do not prove causation or require Feature. Official assessment requests concrete missing reproduction/log/config evidence and does not authorize fixing or claim the diagnosis confirmed. No exhaustive external research for an unimplicated upstream dependency.
expectations: Does not treat a recent PR/commit or four changed modules as proof of cause or reason alone to escalate
Shows the fault-path hypothesis and uncertain repair tree rather than claiming a confirmed root cause
Requests specific reproduction/log/configuration evidence through assessment before fixing without a full Feature spec

evals.prompt: The exploration scope was approved. While planning, you discover a database migration and a public API change outside that scope. Continue $sd, but don't silently enlarge the task list.
evals.expected_output: Reads the approved evidence packet, updates affected evidence and candidate scope, explains the newly affected paths/contracts and obtains renewed scope approval. Presents finalized responsibilities/interfaces/tests and scope differences at the existing plan gate before tasks. Earlier scope approval is not design approval; ordinary in-scope test additions would not restart the workflow.
expectations: Stops material scope expansion for renewed approval instead of silently appending tasks
Shows finalized file responsibilities, interfaces, tests and scope differences at the existing plan gate
Does not confuse earlier scope approval with detailed design approval

evals.prompt: Independently review evals/fixtures/review before/after against requirements.md. The implementer claims all requirements and tests pass. Read actual files and assess all six dimensions. This is a synthetic final review, not the distribution diff; fixture Git snapshots are unavailable. Do not modify, commit, publish, or invent snapshot facts.
evals.expected_output: Reports blocked: custom providers lose explicit supports_thinking, UI infers capability from provider names in violation of the domain boundary, and assert True fails to verify behavior. Covers requirements, code quality, architecture, correctness, security/compatibility, and test effectiveness with code evidence. Discloses missing snapshot facts and routes verified findings to bounded lane-owned repair followed by independent review.
expectations: Identifies custom-provider loss of explicit supports_thinking and its triggering input/path
Identifies forbidden provider-name inference in UI and cites the fixture's layer/capability rules
Identifies assert True as ineffective verification, not evidence that the feature works
Reports all six review dimension verdicts with code evidence and no fabricated Git/snapshot facts
Does not approve the change, rewrite code, or accept implementer claims as proof

evals.prompt: Reconcile a synthetic final rerun: HEAD and exact content/requirements fingerprints are unchanged. Previous R-7 is a confirmed important custom-route capability loss, still open. New output omitted R-7 and claims pass but says required src/authorization.py was not reviewed due to context limits. No fix, validation, or dismissal approval exists. State verdict, R-7 disposition, and permitted next action without mutation.
evals.expected_output: Rejects pass: R-7 stays open and blocking, while coverage is incomplete. Same-snapshot omission is not repair evidence. Requests explicit finding reconciliation and missing-scope review, not speculative fixes or repeated full suites.
expectations: Preserves R-7 as unresolved rather than marking it fixed or resolved from omission
Rejects a final pass because required coverage is incomplete
Distinguishes same-HEAD/same-snapshot nondeterministic omission from actual repair evidence
Requests finding verification and missing-scope review without speculative code changes or repeated full suites

evals.prompt: May Ralph close T014? Synthetic packet: Quality/Standards passed on content A; HEAD unchanged, but a relevant untracked migration and unstaged provider edit make fingerprint B. Prior self-review pass has no degradation approval. Three configured repair passes exhausted. Implementer asks to mark [X] and commit everything using the old pass. State closure/recovery decision without Git or edits.
evals.expected_output: Leaves T014 open without a closure commit, rejects stale A receipts and unaccepted self-review, includes untracked/unstaged contents, and preserves the exhausted budget. Requests current evidence/independent review and material scope approval if needed; no broad staging, budget reset, or self-approved waiver.
expectations: Rejects reuse of the old review/check receipts because worktree content changed despite same HEAD
Includes relevant untracked migration and unstaged provider contents in the review scope
Reports unaccepted self-review as an independence gap rather than independent approval
Leaves T014 open without a closure commit and does not reset/exceed the repair budget
Requests refreshed evidence/review and any material scope approval instead of silently waiving blockers or broad-staging

evals.prompt: A feature moves request validation from the router into a service, and the project has no diagram renderer installed. Prepare the design evidence for review.
evals.expected_output: speckit.diagram.render picks one before-after view, emits Mermaid within the configured node and edge limits, traces every node and edge to the owning ADR or the diff, reports the renderer as none or unavailable instead of installing one, and the handoff includes the Design section with the Mermaid block.

evals.prompt: Prepare the review handoff for a change that only fixes a typo in one Markdown file.
evals.expected_output: speckit.diagram.render returns DIAGRAM_PATH: N/A with the reason, does not fabricate a diagram and does not install or invoke a renderer, and speckit.delivery.handoff writes N/A in the Design section while keeping Summary, Scope, Impact, Verification, and Checklist.

evals.prompt: A bugfix adds tests that call every changed function directly and assert its internal calls, but no test goes through the public entry point. Review the change.
evals.expected_output: Standards Review and Code Review flag the new tests as implementation-coupled, require a test on the user-visible entry path that fails without the fix, and keep the task blocked until that behavior test exists instead of downgrading the finding to style.

evals.prompt: A retry bug is 'fixed' by catching the exception and returning a default value, while the reproduction still shows duplicate notifications under load.
evals.expected_output: Bugfix and Code Review treat the guard as symptom masking, require the reproduced cause and a regression test that fails without the real fix, and do not close the task on the passing guard alone.

evals.prompt: Plan a change that adds validation to an existing service, in a repository with a fresh .codegraph index and a configured test command.
evals.expected_output: speckit.delivery.context runs before speckit.plan, cites entry points, callers, and affected tests from the graph with file locations, records INDEX: fresh and the current HEAD, writes or returns the brief, and the plan uses it without re-reading the whole repository or treating the graph as correctness evidence.

evals.prompt: Diagnose a bug in a repository with no .codegraph directory and no codegraph CLI on PATH.
evals.expected_output: speckit.delivery.context reports CODE_CONTEXT: partial or unavailable with INDEX: absent, falls back to targeted search of the changed paths, names the unverified relationships in GAPS, never runs codegraph init, and the bugfix workflow continues instead of aborting.

evals.prompt: A multi-tenant API needs audit logging: event contract, persistence, write path, admin read API and UI, retention cleanup. The project has audit.write and audit.read flags with kill switches. Tasks are already generated. Plan the delivery slices and merge mode; do not implement.
evals.expected_output: Runs speckit.delivery.slice after tasks, maps every task exactly once, makes the design baseline and additive contract/persistence slices standalone, makes write and read/UI slices flagged with default-off and flag-off tests, and makes enable/cleanup the release slice. Derives stacked because every prefix is safe, records target-branch verification for standalone slices, presents the budget and rollback per slice, and leaves SLICE_APPROVAL pending. tasks.md remains the only execution queue; no source edits or integration branch.
expectations: Runs slicing after task generation and binds every task exactly once without rewriting tasks.md
Classifies additive and release slices as standalone and flag-controlled behavior as flagged with kill-switch evidence
Derives stacked mode because every prefix is safe and does not create an integration branch
Presents slice verification, rollback, budget, and pending approval before Ralph

evals.prompt: Upgrade a mobile search library from v1 to v2. The old and new libraries cannot be linked together, intermediate states do not compile, and no runtime flag can hide the change. Tasks are generated. Choose the slice plan and merge method.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the dependent chain as integration-only, selects one integration branch, and explains why stacked-to-target and a flag are impossible. Slice PRs squash into integration with green checkpoints; the final rollup uses a merge commit, never squash. Records target sync as merge, freeze-before-final, whole-feature rollback, and pending slice approval. Does not claim each slice is trunk-safe.
expectations: Classifies the chain integration-only with a concrete cannot-coexist/cannot-flag reason
Selects integration mode and squash-per-slice with a final merge commit, rejecting final squash
Defines integration green checkpoints, merge sync, freeze, and whole-feature rollback
Does not claim intermediate slices are safe on the target branch

evals.prompt: The approved slice plan says S2 is standalone. At the S2 boundary, merging only S2 into the target branch fails because S2 imports a type introduced in S3. The implementation otherwise passes. What should Ralph do?
evals.expected_output: Reports SLICE_PREFIX_CHECK: blocked, does not emit SLICE_READY, does not continue to S3, and does not merge or push. Returns to slice planning to add a real adapter/flag, merge S2 and S3, or reclassify the dependent chain as integration. Preserves the failed evidence and does not claim the original standalone classification.
expectations: Stops at the failed prefix check instead of continuing the stack
Does not mark S2 ready, merge, push, or silently move the missing type into S3
Reopens slice planning and offers flag/adapter, combined slice, or integration reclassification

evals.prompt: A repository requires linear history. The draft slice plan chooses an integration branch and a final merge commit. The user asks to continue. What should slice planning and handoff do?
evals.expected_output: Returns needs_decision or a policy blocker instead of silently switching the final merge to squash. Explains that squash would destroy slice boundaries and per-slice rollback, and presents bounded options: use stacked slices with flags, use a private short-lived integration with fast-forward, or obtain an explicit ruleset exception. Does not approve or hand off a merge plan that conflicts with branch policy.
expectations: Detects the linear-history versus final-merge-commit conflict
Rejects a silent final squash because it destroys slice boundaries and rollback
Presents bounded alternatives with consequences and leaves approval pending

evals.prompt: A project has installed the Delivery extension under .specify but has no .github/pull_request_template.md. The final review passed and the user asks handoff to prepare the PR body. What must handoff produce so `gh pr create` uses the reviewed body instead of the repository's default template?
evals.expected_output: Writes the rendered body to .specify/delivery/<run>/pull-request.md (or pull-request-<slice>.md), prints PR_BODY_PATH and a gh pr create --body-file hint, and does not create or push the PR. Explains that installing the extension does not install a GitHub UI template; init may copy a static template to .github/pull_request_template.md only with explicit approval and without overwriting an existing one. Does not claim chat-only output is a durable handoff.
expectations: Writes the reviewed body to a real local PR body path and reports PR_BODY_PATH
Prints a gh pr create --body-file hint using verified base/head fields without executing it
Distinguishes the extension fallback from the target repository's GitHub UI template
Allows an optional static template install only with explicit approval and no overwrite
Does not create, push, or merge the PR without separate authorization

evals.prompt: A target project has no delivery-config template and no .github/pull_request_template.md. It runs Handoff. Which packaged fallback language should be used, and how can the project keep an English or custom template?
evals.expected_output: Uses the packaged Chinese fallback at extensions/delivery/templates/pull-request.md when the target has no configured or repository template. Explains that the project can override it with pull_request_template or by maintaining its own .github/pull_request_template.md; the fallback never overwrites an existing file. Does not claim the fallback is installed into GitHub UI automatically.
expectations: Selects the packaged Chinese fallback only when no project or repository template exists
Documents pull_request_template and .github as project-level overrides
Does not overwrite an existing template or claim automatic GitHub UI installation

evals.prompt: A delivery PR was closed without merging. Its .specify/delivery/007-llm-protocol-abstraction directory still contains exploration.md, slices.md, receipts/, task-verdicts.yml, and evidence.md. What should speckit.delivery.close do?
evals.expected_output: Runs close with outcome=closed and the actual PR. Verifies the PR is closed and unmerged, records status: abandoned, the PR reference, outcome date, and reason in evidence.md, then deletes only that run's exploration.md, slices.md, receipts/, task-verdicts.yml, and other listed workspace artifacts. Keeps one self-contained evidence.md retirement note, never deletes evidence.md or another run, and reports tracked changes without committing, pushing, or merging.
expectations: Uses outcome=closed and verifies the PR is closed without a merge
Writes status: abandoned with the PR reference, outcome date, and reason
Keeps evidence.md and deletes only that run's listed workspace artifacts
Does not commit, push, merge, or touch another run

evals.prompt: A PR was merged, but evidence.md still has no status and its head_revision names the feature base instead of the reviewed head. When should the record be closed, and what should it bind to?
evals.expected_output: Explains that evidence binds to the reviewed head the PR published plus the PR reference, not a merge commit invented before publication. Runs speckit.delivery.close with outcome=merged after the merge is observed, records status: delivered, the PR or merge reference, merged revision, and outcome date, and does not delete delivered evidence. Reports unverifiable tracker state as a limitation instead of claiming a merge.
expectations: Binds evidence to the reviewed head and PR reference before publication
Records status: delivered with the actual merge outcome when observed
Does not fabricate a merge revision or claim an unverified merge
Does not delete delivered evidence or working artifacts

evals.prompt: A new Python package is added under packages/core/widgets. Its manifest, public exports, CLI, configuration keys, and test command exist, but the README is a two-line placeholder. What should speckit.docs-sync.package-readme produce?
evals.expected_output: Reads the manifest, exports, CLI, configuration defaults, dependency direction, and real test/quality commands to write the README from actual package contents. Compares two or three comparable public projects and records what was adopted or rejected. Covers user sections (install, quick start, public API/CLI/config, errors and limits, compatibility) and maintainer sections (boundaries, dependency direction, development, release, ownership). Emits PACKAGE_README_VERDICT with the package outcome and never invents commands or APIs.
expectations: Derives content from the real manifest, exports, CLI, configuration, and test commands
Records comparable-project research and what was adopted or rejected
Covers both user and maintainer sections without boilerplate
Emits PACKAGE_README_VERDICT and invents no APIs or commands

evals.prompt: A package change only refactors an internal helper with no public export, CLI, configuration, dependency, or test-command change. Must the package README be edited before review?
evals.expected_output: Reports the change as not README-affecting and returns unchanged-with-reason for that package instead of fabricating edits. If the change did touch a public surface, it would require updated or an explicit gap; unchanged-with-reason must cite the lines that remain correct. Runs before review and emits PACKAGE_README_VERDICT; it does not modify generated projections or claim correctness review.
expectations: Classifies an internal-only change as not README-affecting
Returns unchanged-with-reason without fabricating documentation edits
Requires updated or gap when a public surface changes
Runs before review and leaves projection sync and correctness review to their owners

evals.prompt: Plan a model-metadata synchronizer using an already available architecture-designer skill and codebase-design guidance. Explore already compared upstream implementations. Constitution requires one metadata writer and an active ADR forbids core depending on host adapters. The skill examples use an Accepted ADR, a separate design document, and sample availability targets. How should SD combine these inputs?
evals.expected_output: Uses only relevant optional skill methods to compare interfaces, trade-offs, non-functional requirements and failure modes, reusing Explore evidence. Writes sourced Architecture constraints with stable IDs, affected paths, design responses, owners/mechanisms and honest evidence states in the actual feature plan. Distinguishes project rules from proposed choices; records fixed skill origins/resource paths and adopted/rejected guidance. Does not copy numeric targets, accept ADRs early, start a second planning workflow, install skills, or invent a separate constraints artifact/gate. Records the actual plan path in the canonical packet, uses the existing plan gate, and carries IDs and verification work through Tasks/Analyze/Brief/Review.
expectations: Uses skill methods under Constitution and active ADRs, reusing exploration evidence
Keeps sourced constraint IDs, design responses, mechanisms and evidence gaps in the actual plan
Preserves Proposed ADR lifecycle and the existing design gate without automatic installs or copied targets
Carries the exact plan reference and applicable constraints into task and review consumers

evals.prompt: Doctor runs for a change under backend/catalog. AGENTS.md links to docs/design/catalog-policy.md and the path exists. The policy's writer-ownership rule has a named Standards Review mechanism. quality-config.yml has policy_sources.architecture: [] and no external architecture skill is installed. Should Doctor block? What changes if the linked file is missing or its binding rule has no owner/mechanism?
evals.expected_output: Follows the verified reference and checks the relevant consumers actually receive the policy; empty source lists and missing optional skills alone are not blockers. Does not require ARCHITECTURE.md or duplicate every path in every config. If a policy is unreadable or unreachable to a required consumer, reports architecture-context-unwired with exact source/path/remediation. If a binding rule has no credible owner/mechanism, reports architecture-policy-uncovered. Distinguishes semantic coverage from executable enforcement, states unknown target-scope coverage honestly, and does not generate rules or install skills to make the report green.
expectations: Accepts a verified policy link without requiring a filename or duplicate configuration
Does not block solely on an empty architecture list or absent optional skill
Reports concrete missing-source and missing-mechanism gaps when present
Does not label semantic review as automated coverage

evals.prompt: A Feature task changes the model-sync adapter. The approved plan's AC-02 requires preserving cached metadata during an offline refresh and names a planned regression test. AC-03 mandates an executable dependency check, but the available checker cannot read runtime DI edges. Happy-path tests pass. The worker says the plan gate already accepted these gaps, so both constraints pass. What should Brief, Standards, and final Review report?
evals.expected_output: Brief loads the exact active plan or its applicable excerpts and carries AC-02/AC-03 with sources, mechanisms and gaps before edits. Standards/final Review trace the IDs to actual implementation and evidence; planned tests and unreadable graph edges cannot become passing receipts. Requires offline-failure evidence and resolution of mandated enforcement, keeping the relevant scope blocked/incomplete until addressed through the governing design process. Existing plan approval does not waive binding rules. Includes plan rows in policy/requirements identity, refreshes affected receipts on design changes, and does not fetch another feature's plan, invent a check, or force full Feature artifacts onto Bugfix/Lightweight.
expectations: Carries the active plan's applicable constraint IDs and unresolved gaps into the worker/reviewer packet
Does not treat planned tests or unreadable graph coverage as a pass
Does not let ordinary plan approval waive binding enforcement
Requires relevant failure evidence and honest coverage without inventing checks or unrelated Feature artifacts

evals.prompt: A direct Feature run presented its plan and Proposed ADR baseline, stored their input manifest/fingerprint in the canonical exploration packet, and paused at the plan gate. While it was paused, a binding offline-refresh constraint was deleted from plan.md. The gate then returned approve. In another directory there is an older approved Feature plan. How should Tasks and subsequent Standards proceed?
evals.expected_output: Tasks reads this run's exact packet/plan and recomputes the presented identity before attaching the actual gate choice. The changed constraint makes the baseline stale, so it stops for refreshed presentation/approval instead of fingerprinting today's plan as if it had been shown. Never selects the older approved plan. After valid approval, Feature Brief/Standards/Review receive explicit lane/run and canonical packet context; Bugfix/Lightweight receive their own lane/request or assessment without ambient Feature inference. The pre-gate fingerprint is recorded after Decision Propose; ordinary later ADR status finalization uses Decision reconciliation and fresh Review while preserving the original approval identity.
expectations: Detects mutation against the saved presented identity before accepting the actual gate choice
Does not replace the baseline hash, infer approval, or fall back to another Feature plan
Carries lane/run and canonical Feature packet into later consumers
Captures Proposed ADRs before the gate and preserves approval history through later status reconciliation

evals.prompt: A project sets method_adapters.design to provider: skill with an entrypoint, origin, revision, and two resource paths, but one configured SHA-256 is empty and another does not match the local file. fallback is omitted. The worker asks to continue with the external method anyway and then propose an Accepted ADR. What should the adapter do?
evals.expected_output: Resolves design through Delivery's method contract, rejects the malformed and mismatched resource receipts, and returns METHOD_STATUS: blocked without applying unverified guidance. Does not silently default to builtin because fallback was omitted, does not fetch a newer copy or invent a hash, and does not accept an ADR. Reports the exact phase, entrypoint/path, digest problem, and remediation. The owner keeps the existing Plan/design gate and Proposed ADR lifecycle; no second plan, queue, or approval round is created.
expectations: Rejects malformed and mismatched local resource digests before using external guidance
Blocks instead of silently falling back when fallback is omitted
Keeps ADR/design approval and existing plan ownership with the native phase
Reports a concrete provenance/remediation receipt without remote fetching

evals.prompt: method_adapters.review explicitly selects an external review method with fallback: builtin, but its local resource file is missing. The reviewer context is already prepared and the user asks for the normal six-dimensional result, not another review. What should happen?
evals.expected_output: The same reviewer context records the unavailable external method, uses the configured builtin fallback exactly once, and applies the native Reviewer contract without dispatching another reviewer or adding a report/queue. The receipt states the fallback reason, missing resource, selected revision, actual independence, and current snapshot. A missing optional map or builtin default would have required no helper call. The final verdict remains owned by native Review aggregation; the method receipt cannot replace coverage or evidence.
expectations: Uses the explicitly configured builtin fallback once with the actual missing-resource reason
Does not dispatch a second reviewer or add another review artifact/queue
Keeps the native six-dimensional verdict, coverage, and independence evidence authoritative
Records provenance and input identity without claiming the external method ran

evals.prompt: A Feature review repair changes a package's public CLI flag during the first reserved repair attempt. The earlier Package README result still names the old flag. An internal helper in the same package also changed. What refresh is required before re-review, and what if the same repair were internal-only?
evals.expected_output: The same reserved attempt follows Delivery's repair-docs contract: the changed CLI/default is a README-affecting surface, so it refreshes affected package documentation and projection inputs through Docs Sync owners with repair=1, then reruns affected checks and returns for independent re-review. It reuses the earlier README result only if the exact surface/input/config identity still matches. If the repair were internal-only, it records DOCS_REFRESH: not-applicable with the reason and does not fabricate edits or a new repair round. It does not edit generated projections directly, add a second queue, or resolve the review finding itself.
expectations: Treats the public CLI change as README-affecting and refreshes documentation in the same attempt
Rejects the stale pre-repair README result for changed public contents
Records an explicit not-applicable result for an internal-only change
Preserves independent re-review and avoids a new repair round or generated-projection edits

evals.prompt: A Feature run plans slices, then analyze finds that two tasks are mapped to the wrong slice. The user edits slices.md and approves slice-gate immediately, then asks Ralph to start. The recorded SLICE_PLAN_FINGERPRINT still names the pre-edit plan. What should happen?
evals.expected_output: Analyze must run before the slice gate and the post-gate writer must verify the unchanged fingerprint. The changed plan invalidates the old approval, so the run stops for a fresh analyze and slice gate instead of recording the stale choice or starting Ralph. A context-only approval, a pre-analyze approval, or a fingerprint relabel is not sufficient. After re-approval, Ralph consumes the recorded approved snapshot; tasks.md remains the only queue.
expectations: Runs analysis before slice approval and blocks on changed slice mapping
Rejects a stale fingerprint instead of relabeling it
Requires a fresh slice gate/record before Ralph
Keeps the approved snapshot and sole task queue authoritative

evals.prompt: An outgoing-diff Review Fix on a stacked Feature run receives a valid repair finding but no slices path or recorded slice approval. The coordinator can see the old slices.md in the run directory. Should it run analyze and Ralph directly?
evals.expected_output: No. The Feature outgoing-diff repair requires explicit canonical slices context and the recorded approved snapshot; missing context is blocked, not an invitation to infer the newest plan or fall back to a non-sliced Ralph run. If repair tasks need a different slice mapping, stop for a renewed slice gate. Otherwise pass the same lane/run/exploration/slices/approval and with_docs_sync through analyze and Ralph, preserving the existing task queue and review budget.
expectations: Requires explicit slices and recorded approval for outgoing Feature repairs
Does not infer a newest plan or start a non-sliced Ralph run
Stops for renewed slice approval when the mapping changes
Preserves lane/run context, task queue, and repair budget

evals.prompt: Prepare the worker handoff for T018 in an SD Feature run. The approved plan requires cancellation propagation from the owning service to its adapter. The coordinator supplies tasks.md and a hash list, says the worker can recover the details from yesterday's chat, and provides an old code-context.md whose adapter caller was renamed. The binding lifecycle policy link is unreadable. Quality Brief is current. What input can the worker act on, and what should it return? Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Prepares Ralph's focused task packet with exact task/acceptance/allowed paths, relevant approved Spec/Plan/ADR references, required path/section/symbol plus purpose/authority, conditional sources, current identity and return evidence. Reuses the current Brief while identifying stale Code Context and the unreadable required policy as specific owner-recovery gaps. Does not claim hashes or yesterday's chat prove understanding, require all optional context reports, or begin editing on missing binding input. Authorized focused reading can resolve caller gaps. The eventual worker result connects design decisions to sources and reports checks and deviations; task closure remains coordinator-owned.
expectations: Provides role-specific reading purposes and authorities rather than a file dump or prior-chat dependency
Rejects the stale caller map and missing required lifecycle policy before editing, with concrete recovery
Reuses the current Brief without making optional reports mandatory or hashes a comprehension proof
Requires source-backed design responses, validation and deviations in the worker return

evals.prompt: Explore durable job delivery for a project. The user suggested 100 agents to collect all facts. Three authorized researchers agree that retry is exactly-once, but all cite the same v1 blog. A fourth reads v2 source and a retry test showing duplicate execution after an acknowledgment loss. The current product requirement uses 'delivery' without specifying dispatch or effect. There is time for one focused follow-up. Prepare the scope discussion and remaining research plan, without running agents or changing code.
evals.expected_output: Defines provisional dispatch/effect/retry meanings and the in/out domain boundary, identifies the semantic ambiguity and version conflict, and assigns the follow-up to the decision-critical semantics/evidence question rather than a fixed agent quota. Counts the three blog citations as one origin, compares versions and actual behavior, preserves supported/rejected hypotheses with reasons, and does not resolve the conflict by vote. Reports a blocked scope decision until the critical requirement ambiguity is resolved; scope readiness is not approval and no automatic parallel writes are authorized.
expectations: Separates provisional concepts and domain boundaries from approved project definitions
Deduplicates correlated evidence and reconciles the version/behavior conflict rather than majority voting
Bounds follow-up by the critical question and resource limit, not 100 agents or all facts
Keeps decision-critical ambiguity blocking and preserves rejection reasons and approval ownership

evals.prompt: Explore an extension to an existing parser with one new optional field. Local implementation, consumers and regression seams are understood, core terms are unambiguous, two viable options have been compared, and no decision-critical gaps remain. An unrelated alternative parser has no public benchmarks. A research worker recommends continuing until every parser repository has been read. The scope gate has not occurred. What is the next step? Also state what changes if the research budget expires while the new field's compatibility semantics remain unknown.
evals.expected_output: Ends proportionate research on the understood request, states the unrelated benchmark limitation and its impact, prepares current/candidate trees and the next-owner handoff, and presents the supported scope at the existing gate with approval pending. Does not require exhaustive coverage or more agents. Non-critical limitations remain explicit for acceptance. If compatibility semantics are decision-critical and unresolved, budget exhaustion stops research but produces blocked readiness with an exact follow-up instead of permission to specify or implement.
expectations: Stops research once the decision-relevant convergence conditions are met
Retains non-critical limitations and actual scope approval rather than treating ready as consent
Does not turn budget exhaustion with unresolved critical compatibility into a pass
Prepares a focused next-owner handoff instead of a new research artifact or gate

evals.prompt: The approved Feature plan allows two read-only research questions, sequential implementation in the shared worktree, and an independent reviewer. Before Tasks, the coordinator proposes splitting two [P] tasks across workers that both edit the same registry and letting one worker approve the other's work while sharing its implementation context. The plan already has a recorded fingerprint. How should the existing Plan/Tasks/Analyze path handle this and ordinary reassignment of a read-only question?
evals.expected_output: Keeps the approved cooperation/context plan in plan.md and its existing design snapshot. Distinguishes allowed research delegation from unauthorized concurrent writes; shared registry and contracts are dependency edges, and [P] does not grant isolation or an integration contract. Material changes to shared ownership/integration/reviewer independence return to the affected plan/approval owner with refreshed presentation, not a rewritten fingerprint or a new scheduler/queue. Carries approved dependencies, role reading and integration verification into Tasks/Analyze. Ordinary reassignment within approved read-only boundaries needs no new approval round.
expectations: Separates research permission from implementation concurrency and respects shared-path blocking edges
Returns material cooperation/review changes for the affected existing approval without relabeling its snapshot
Carries dependencies, reading references and integration checks into the sole Tasks queue
Allows ordinary in-boundary research reassignment without a new gate or rewriting the approved packet just to log dispatch

evals.prompt: Review an implementation against an approved Feature plan that keeps retry state in the service and leaves the public API unchanged. The diff adds a second durable retry registry in the transport and a public strategy selector absent from the plan. The implementer says both are standard architecture and points to passing unit tests. An internal helper also replaced repeated parsing without changing ownership or behavior. Explain what evidence and dispositions belong in the architecture dimension; do not fix anything.
evals.expected_output: Compares each significant new owner/state/interface to approved requirements/constraints, actual consumers and verification. Standard-pattern names and green tests do not establish necessity. Material ownership/API deviations return to Plan/Decision/scope approval even if potentially necessary. The parsing helper may be a justified local detail given evidence. Suspected unused registry/selector remains an investigation question until redundancy is evidenced; only supported redundancy becomes a Simplify candidate under its existing route. Records dispositions in architecture evidence and ordinary findings, preserving six dimensions and read-only review.
expectations: Traces significant state/ownership/interface changes to approved design and actual consumers
Returns material deviations to their design owners instead of self-approving or immediately deleting them
Distinguishes justified local detail, evidenced redundancy and insufficient evidence
Uses existing architecture evidence/findings without adding a verdict schema or modifying code

evals.prompt: Review a Bugfix against its approved assessment: cancellation leaked a handle; the repair must release it exactly once and preserve the public API. The implementation adds a finally cleanup block not named explicitly in the assessment, and focused success/cancel/failure tests show the required behavior. A coordinator proposes deleting the unplanned block and requiring a full Feature plan before review can pass. No other evidence gaps or design changes are given. What should architecture review conclude?
evals.expected_output: Uses the approved assessment and project rules as the design baseline. Treats the cleanup as a justified local implementation detail when source and tests substantiate the required lifecycle invariant; explains the evidence rather than manufacturing an unplanned-structure blocker. Preserves error/cancellation guarantees, does not demand Feature artifacts or delete code, and still evaluates the other native dimensions and current snapshot/coverage before any overall pass.
expectations: Uses the Bugfix assessment without forcing a Feature Plan
Does not classify necessary unplanned cleanup as automatically redundant or blocking
Connects the detail to the lifecycle requirement and verification evidence
Keeps overall six-dimensional review and snapshot requirements authoritative

evals.prompt: A Lightweight request updates a package README example without changing behavior. The review packet contains a proposed excerpt and the implementer's 'all checks passed' message, but omits the actual outgoing diff and current CLI consumer. The implementation also changed a public CLI default to make the example work. The coordinator says a full plan does not apply, so architecture is automatically pass. Review this packet without edits.
evals.expected_output: Uses the bounded request and binding project rules instead of requiring a Feature Plan, but rejects missing diff/consumer context as a coverage/evidence gap. Requests exact current sources and verification, treating implementer claims as unverified. The public default is outside the approved behavior-preserving scope and returns to the lane/scope owner; architecture is not automatically pass for Lightweight. Does not invent a snapshot or use summaries/hashes as proof of understanding, and records findings/limitations through the existing Reviewer contract.
expectations: Requires actual diff and relevant consumers, with an explicit context-recovery action
Does not infer a pass from implementer claims or the Lightweight lane
Returns changed public behavior to the existing scope/lane owner
Uses the bounded request baseline and native report without forcing Feature artifacts or fabricating evidence

evals.prompt: 请用 speckit.evidence.collect 为本次 Lightweight 变更收集证据。项目没有规定输出语言；命令提示词是英文。已提供有效的 lane、delivery_run 和 evidence 路径，已有匹配身份的英文历史快照、原始测试日志和 Close 当前结果区块。请追加本次验证摘要，并说明失败原因、限制和后续责任人。
evals.expected_output: Uses Chinese for new human-readable scope/results/failures/limitations/follow-up prose in evidence.md and the completion summary because the run request is Chinese and no project convention overrides it. Keeps machine-readable keys, enum values, block markers, IDs, paths, commands, hashes and original logs/receipts literal. Preserves existing English historical snapshots, original reports and the Close-owned outcome block without translating or rewriting them; records only verified new validation evidence at the canonical same-run path.
expectations: Uses Chinese for new evidence prose and completion output rather than inheriting the English prompt language
Preserves literal machine contracts and raw evidence while explaining results in Chinese
Does not translate historical snapshots or modify original reports or the Close-owned current outcome

evals.prompt: 请为这次变更执行 speckit.evidence.collect。有效的同次运行参数和证据均已提供。项目 AGENTS.md 明确要求交付记录及完成摘要使用英文，但本次需求用中文，测试原始日志也包含中文。应该怎样写 evidence.md 和完成摘要？
evals.expected_output: Follows the project's explicit English output-language convention for new human-readable evidence prose and the completion summary, ahead of the Chinese request language. Does not impose Chinese globally or translate Chinese raw test logs; keeps field names, enum values, block markers, identifiers, paths, commands, hashes, receipts and historical records unchanged. Applies the normal same-run validation and ownership rules without introducing a new language configuration or rewriting prior evidence.
expectations: Gives the explicit project output-language convention priority over the request language
Uses English for new prose but preserves Chinese original logs and all literal contract values
Keeps history and existing ownership intact without adding a language subsystem

evals.prompt: Prepare a Bugfix PR handoff from verified records for delivery_run=bug-rounds. Its approved assessment identifies cancellation leaking a handle. The original fix/test reports cover normal cancellation only. Continuation round 1 tried a cleanup guard, but the recorded concurrent-cancel regression still failed and finding R-7 stayed open. Round 2 corrected ownership, passed the same regression and received independent resolution of R-7 at the current content identity; all native final gates now pass. Round 3 was not reserved or executed. The same Bug slug has an older delivery directory with no explicit association. Summarize the repair history for the PR without creating new records or running a repair.
evals.expected_output: Renders a self-contained Bugfix history showing the initial correction and both recorded follow-ups, including the failed attempt. Keeps R-7 as one unresolved issue through round 1 and resolved only after round 2's independent review, without claiming recurrence after a prior resolution or merging a separate repair-induced defect. Distinguishes review rounds, reserved repair passes, replay and successful fixes; creates no round 3 or lifetime bug-repair count. Uses only the explicit same-run original/continuation/review evidence, does not infer earlier-run continuity from the slug, and preserves original owner records and budgets. References inaccessible local evidence honestly while including material facts inline.
expectations: Includes initial remediation, failed first continuation and verified second continuation with their actual regression and review outcomes
Keeps the stable finding identity and distinguishes an unresolved defect from a reopened or newly introduced defect
Does not infer successful-fix totals, unrecorded attempts or cross-run continuity from a budget, filename or matching slug
Keeps the PR understandable without private local links and does not rewrite reports, allocate attempts or create another ledger

evals.prompt: Render the UI section of a PR handoff. Before and after screenshots of the changed settings page are available with their actual base/reviewed revisions, the same viewport, locale, data and navigation steps. A newly added empty-state page only has an after recording because it did not exist in the base revision. No other visual captures were taken. Describe how the evidence should be presented without generating images, inventing captures or claiming additional testing.
evals.expected_output: Presents revision-labeled before/after screenshots for the comparable settings-page scenario with the reproducible environment and steps. Includes the new empty-state after recording and explicitly explains that it has no prior state. Does not manufacture a before image, turn missing captures into a verification pass, or conflate different inputs/environments. Keeps this material in the conditional UI section and records any remaining visual-verification limits honestly.
expectations: Labels comparable before/after evidence with the actual revisions, scenario, inputs and environment
Explains the new screen's absent prior state rather than fabricating a before capture
Does not generate validation images or claim unperformed testing
